chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Two twigs are placed for the deceased, one on the right and the other on the left.
He said: He said: The twig benefits the believer and the disbeliever.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the twigs placed for the deceased in the grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the placement of two *jaridat* (twigs or palm fronds) on the right and left of the deceased in the grave. While the physical act is specific, the Imam clarifies that the spiritual benefit of this twig extends universally to both the believer (*mu'min*) and the disbeliever (*kafir*), highlighting a shared aspect of comfort in the intermediate realm (*barzakh*) regardless of ultimate faith status.
